transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-12-15 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Reed (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (CISO, Crestview), Miguel Torres (Cloud Architect, Crestview), Jenna Park (Security Engineer, Crestview), Robert Han (Product)

Summary: short security-focused deep dive on private VPC deployment and network controls. Discussed RBAC/SSO, KMS/HSM, audit logs, ingress/egress, and firewalling.

[00:00] Alex Reed: all right folks, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account, we also have Samir and Priya from our solutions team. thanks for making time.
[00:10] Karen Liu: thanks Alex, we wanna go deep on the network stuff today - specifically how you isolate traffic and what controls we have on egress. also need to validate KMS options, and, uh, audit log delivery to Splunk.
[00:21] Samir Patel: yep, totally, we'll map that end to end. quick agenda: control-plane vs data-plane, private endpoints, egress patterns, firewalling and IDS, plus key management and logging.
[00:32] Miguel Torres: just to call out, we have a pretty strict baseline: no public IPs on compute, all outbound goes through our egress proxy, deep packet inspection for https is handled upstream, and any external connections need to be whitelisted by infra.
[00:45] Priya Desai: understoond, that's exactly the model our private deployment supports. to confirm, Redwood Private runs the control plane in our managed region and places the data-plane components in your VPC - no public internet on the data-plane by default.
[00:58] Jenna Park: how do we handle updates/patching if there's no public IPs?
[01:04] Samir Patel: good question - typical pattern is to allow egress to a very small set of endpoints for OS/package updates via your egress proxy or via an internal artifact repo. alternatively we support pulling updates through a NAT with strict egress rules and cert pinning. note that the control-plane funnels model scheduling and config, but payloads and KV cache stay inside your VPC.
[01:30] Karen Liu: when you say control-plane, are we talking about Redwood owning any keys or does customer manage the KMS?
[01:36] Alex Reed: by default we support customer-managed keys (CMK) in major clouds - so AWS KMS, Google KMS, or customer HSM. envelope encryption used for model artifacts and logs; Redwood never has the plaintext key. we also offer an option for Redwood-managed keys for non-sensitive workloads.
[01:54] Miguel Torres: can you walk that flow? e.g., a token coming into the private endpoint, where's it decrypted, how's it logged?
[02:01] Priya Desai: sure, high level: request enters via a PrivateLink / VPC Endpoint -> hits data-plane compute (no public ip) -> data-plane uses a local encryption library to call customer KMS using the VPC endpoint to the KMS service or via a customer VPN to an HSM in-prem -> data is processed and KV cache is stored encrypted at rest. logs are forwarded to our local log forwarder and then sent to your Splunk endpoint over a dedicated outbound connection. (crosstalk)
[02:28] Jenna Park: sorry - you said private link - do you support AWS PrivateLink and GCP private service connect?
[02:33] Samir Patel: yes, we support PrivateLink for AWS, Private Service Connect for GCP, and Azure Private Endpoint. we also can use IPsec or AWS Transit Gateway for hybrid on-prem setups.
[02:42] Karen Liu: what about firewalling - security groups vs NACLs vs perimeter firewall? we prefer centralized firewalling and expect egress allow-listing only.
[02:51] Priya Desai: customers typically implement layered controls: security groups close to instances, NACLs for subnet-level controls, and a centralized firewall or NGFW at the egress. Redwood supports that - the data-plane components are configured to operate within those constraints. we provide a recommended set of security group rules and ports.
[03:10] Miguel Torres: do you require any inbound ports? our security policy is no inbound from internet.
[03:15] Alex Reed: no, for private deployments there are zero inbound public ports required. all inbound is via VPC endpoint or peering. only the control-plane communicates to the data-plane over a mutually authenticated TLS channel on private network paths.
[03:28] Jenna Park: audit logs - we need to retain all admin actions and request metadata for seven years and ship to Splunk with guaranteed ordering. can you support that?
[03:38] Samir Patel: yes, we can forward structured audit logs - admin actions, model versions, request metadata - to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Sumo, Datadog). retention policies can be configured on your side; we also keep a copy in the local encrypted store. we support signable audit trails and export in NDJSON.
[03:58] Karen Liu: NDJSON okay. what level of identity mapping do you provide? we use SSO SAML + SCIM provisioning via Okta and need role-based access controls mapped to our AD groups.
[04:09] Priya Desai: we integrate with SAML SSO (Okta, Azure AD) and support SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is plumbed to map AD/Okta groups to Redwood roles like admin, auditor, operator. we can also do just-in-time role mapping if needed.
[04:26] Robert Han: curious about network egress restrictions: we want to prevent every outbound call except to our artifact repo and KMS - can Redwood run with a fully restricted egress policy?
[04:36] Samir Patel: yes. we have customers who run with allow-listing for only required endpoints: KMS, control-plane endpoints, artifact repos, and monitoring endpoints. note that if you restrict DNS or certificate revocation endpoints you may impact TLS flows - we document exact FQDNs and IP ranges.
[04:56] Miguel Torres: will you provide those FQDNs/IPs? we prefer IP ranges to lock in NACLs.
[05:02] Alex Reed: absolutely - we'll share the published control-plane IP ranges and TLS cert fingerprints. for larger deployments we can do a dedicated Transit Gateway peering so we don't rely on ephemeral public IPs.
[05:15] Jenna Park: thread: HSM integration - we must keep key material in our HSM, not in cloud KMS. do you support on-prem HSM via VPN?
[05:24] Priya Desai: yes, we support bringing-your-own-HSM. data-plane can access on-prem HSM over an IPSec tunnel or private interconnect; we support PKCS#11 flows and wrap keys with customer master key from the HSM. performance note: HSM calls add latency so we recommend caching wrapped DEKs locally in the data-plane with appropriate TTLs.
[05:48] Miguel Torres: how do you attest that logs haven't been tampered with?
[05:52] Samir Patel: we support append-only audit logs with signing and can forward checksum manifests to your Splunk; we also support pushing signed manifests to an S3 bucket you control.
[06:05] Karen Liu: compliance artifacts - SOC 2 and ISO 27001 evidence - can you provide the report and the scope?
[06:11] Alex Reed: yes, I'll share our SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates and control mappings. we also have a security whitepaper for private deployments that details the network flows, TLS, key management, and recommended firewall rules.
[06:24] Jenna Park: SLA questions - if the control-plane is multitenant, how do you guarantee latency/availability for our workloads?
[06:31] Samir Patel: good question - we offer dedicated capacity options and private control-plane variants for enterprise that provide isolation and SLO-backed throughput. for private VPC deployments we can negotiate reserved pools for your tenant.
[06:44] Miguel Torres: any differences between AWS and GCP in terms of network implementation?
[06:49] Priya Desai: minor differences: AWS uses PrivateLink endpoints and VPC Endpoints, GCP uses Private Service Connect; the principles are the same but the implementation details vary slightly. for cross-cloud we recommend Transit Gateway or a SD-WAN overlay.
[07:03] Robert Han: also need to confirm whether Redwood's agents open any ephemeral outbound connections to random CDNs etc for models - we've seen vendors do that and it's a no.
[07:13] Alex Reed: we never call arbitrary CDNs from the data-plane. any model artifacts or tokenizer downloads are pulled from your artifact repo or from pre-approved Redwood artifact endpoints which we can host inside your VPC for full air-gap.
[07:26] Jenna Park: what about IDS/IPS - can you integrate with our managed detection service?
[07:31] Samir Patel: yes, logs and VPC flow logs can be forwarded to your IDS. we can also run host-based agents on data-plane nodes if needed.
[07:40] Miguel Torres: do you support traffic mirroring for packet capture?
[07:44] Priya Desai: on AWS we support VPC Traffic Mirroring to your monitoring fleet; similar mirroring exists on other clouds. note there are cost and privacy implications.
[07:55] Karen Liu: incident response - if there's a compromise, what's the playbook and RTO?
[08:01] Alex Reed: we have a documented IR playbook for private customers. typical steps: isolate data-plane, rotate keys (CMK/HSM), preserve audit trail, and failover to a recovery cluster. RTO depends on the size of the deployment and agreed SLAs; we'll share example timelines.
[08:18] Robert Han: tooling-wise we want per-route cost & latency breakdown for audits - is that available in your console for private deployments?
[08:26] Samir Patel: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-model dashboards for private setups too; we can configure read-only auditor roles for your compliance team.
[08:38] Miguel Torres: curious about head-of-line blocking and batching - if we enable aggressive batching to save cost, we need predictable latency for some endpoints. can you pin models to low-latency nodes?
[08:49] Priya Desai: yes, routing policies let you select latency-priority pools vs cost-priority pools. you can also pin endpoints to dedicated GPUs.
[08:58] Karen Liu: we need to test network egress in a controlled way - what does your pilot look like?
[09:04] Alex Reed: pilot is typically 2-3 nodes in your stage VPC, we push a small traffic profile, validate KMS flows, audit forwarding, and run connectivity tests. Priya will run the connectivity checklist with Miguel.
[09:17] Jenna Park: any gotchas on DNS? we keep internal DNS strictly locked down.
[09:21] Samir Patel: ensure your VPC endpoints can resolve the necessary FQDNs - we provide a list. we also support VPC endpoints that avoid DNS resolution to the public internet by using private hosted zones.
[09:34] Miguel Torres: encryption-at-rest specifics - which volumes and DBs are encrypted and with which keys?
[09:39] Priya Desai: all disk volumes, KV cache, and any persistent model artifacts are encrypted with DEKs wrapped by your CMK/HSM. we also support FIPS 140-2 validated crypto stacks on request.
[09:56] Karen Liu: can you do a short network flow diagram in the follow-up doc so our network team can sign off?
[10:01] Alex Reed: yes, we'll include diagrams showing control-plane, data-plane, VPC endpoints, NATs, and egress firewalling.
[10:08] Robert Han: licensing/policy - how do we ensure audits for third parties that access metadata?
[10:13] Samir Patel: we track principal-to-action mappings in the audit logs; you can configure least-privilege roles and require MFA for admin actions.
[10:24] Miguel Torres: on monitoring, what metrics do you emit that we can ingest?
[10:28] Priya Desai: latency per route, CPU/GPU utilization, memory, KV hit-rate, request QPS, error rates, and per-token cost metrics. we can push these to Prometheus/Grafana stacks or cloud monitoring.
[10:44] Jenna Park: any recommendations for firewall rules to block risky egress like CRL/OCSP? we need to allow OCSP but log it heavily.
[10:52] Samir Patel: allow OCSP endpoints but only to specific FQDNs; we include certificate pinned fingerprints in the follow-up.
[11:02] Karen Liu: vendor risk - what's your third-party supply chain? do you use public model hubs that could bring in dependencies?
[11:10] Alex Reed: we curate model artifacts for private deployments and can host vetted model binaries inside your VPC or on your artifact repo. we can also provide SBOM-like manifests for binaries.
[11:22] Miguel Torres: for network hardening, we want host-based firewalls and minimal OS surface. do you support custom AMIs/base images?
[11:28] Priya Desai: yes, we can use your hardened images or provide ours that meet CIS benchmarks; we also support immutable infrastructure patterns.
[11:37] Robert Han: last question - can we run Redwood fully air-gapped?
[11:40] Samir Patel: yes - we offer an on-prem package that can be fully air-gapped, though it requires additional timelines for model updates and operational support; we'll include those constraints in the follow-up.
[11:52] Alex Reed: great, recapping next steps: I'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts and the private deployment whitepaper with diagrams; Priya will coordinate the connectivity checklist with Miguel; Miguel to share VPC details; we'll schedule the pilot run.
[12:05] Karen Liu: thanks everyone, that covers it. we'll review the artifacts and get back on the pilot scheduling.
[12:10] Alex Reed: thanks, end call.

Notes on transcript quality: some terms transcribed as V-PC or K-V cache; occasional filler words and small mislabels.
